A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RG-VFM work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material across pagination changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original checkerboard-generation, MOF structure-prediction, and protein-generation results in Section 5, with additional experiments in Appendices E and F.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports a qualitative comparison of two training-loss normalization choices in Section 5.1.

M1.justification: The RG-VFM objective family, intrinsic and extrinsic variants, and rotational-loss adaptations of MOFFlow, QFlow, and ReQFlow are retained. The new pseudocode documents existing procedures without establishing a method redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate spherical and hyperbolic checkerboards, the Boyd et al. MOF dataset, and filtered Protein Data Bank structures. The normalization comparison uses retained task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments: CFM/VFM/RFM for checkerboards, DiffCSP/MOFFlow for MOFs, and RFDiffusion, Genie2, FoldFlow2, FrameFlow, QFlow, and ReQFlow for proteins. Appendix comparisons retain their original comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 newly reports a controlled training comparison between sigma_t(x)=1 and sigma_t(x)=1-t. Existing benchmark metrics, sample sizes, splits, and training budgets are retained; the PDFs do not establish that the original benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds a brief sensitivity analysis asking whether time-dependent loss normalization affects synthetic results. The Laplace-posterior analysis in Appendix E.4 and integration-step study in Appendix F.2 already appear in v2 and remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The existing plus/minus reporting in Tables 1, 3, and 6 is unchanged. V3 adds no seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the normalization comparison.

E6.justification: The new qualitative finding is that sigma_t(x)=1 and sigma_t(x)=1-t produced negligible differences in the synthetic experiments. Numerical results in Tables 1–3, 6, and 7 and the plotted experimental results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The propositions, curvature relationships, definitions, and proofs in Section 4 and Appendices C–D are retained. New Equation (6) explicitly presents the existing Euclidean mean-to-velocity relationship, while the constant-sigma assumption was already stated in Appendix D.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about extending VFM to manifolds, relating its objective to RFM through curvature, and improving material and protein generation. Reordering the motivation does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: Sections 3.1 and 4.2 add an embedding-dimension qualification for the extrinsic variant and explicit computational-cost comparisons with VFM/RFM. V3 also notes the experiments' emphasis on constant-curvature manifolds; existing result interpretations and the closed-form-geodesic limitation remain.

D1.justification: V3 adds training/sampling pseudocode and identifies sigma_t(x)=1 for reported synthetic results and 1-t for material/protein experiments. The latter disclosure is not reconciled with the unweighted rotational loss still printed in Appendix F.1. Hardware, budgets, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged. Discussion of VFM applications moves from the background into the introduction, while positioning relative to VFM, RFM, and existing material/protein models is retained.

P1.justification: V3 revises the abstract and introduction's ordering, relocates background discussion, clarifies intrinsic/extrinsic terminology, and expands explanations of sampling and normalization. The section hierarchy remains stable, and the header changes from an arXiv preprint to an ICLR 2026 conference paper.

P2.justification: V3 adds two side-by-side algorithm displays in Section 3.1 and six in Appendix D.2, causing local text and float relocation. Existing Figures 1–17 and Tables 1–7 retain their content and basic design.

improvement.justification: The added pseudocode and clearer explanations of the two variants make v3 easier to understand and implement. Gains are limited: benchmark results and proofs remain unchanged, the normalization sensitivity finding is only qualitative, and the new time-normalization disclosure remains inconsistent with the loss printed in Appendix F.1.
